candidates.source_name: BQK — Institucionet Financiare të Licencuara (register of licensed/registered financial institutions, incl. non-bank PSPs/EMIs)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative and periodically re-published list (PDF per revision date) naming every licensed non-bank actor in Kosovo: IFJB (institucione financiare jobankare), payment institutions, e-money institutions, money-transfer companies and exchange offices. This is the master actor map for the whole non-bank payments cell and the seed for snowballing to each actor's own site.

Note: direct PDF fetch returned HTTP 403 in this run (bot defence) — use a browser-like client.

negative_findings.description: Searches in sq (bankomat, kompani jo-bankare) and en for an independent/white-label ATM deploying company in Kosovo returned only bank-owned ATM networks (Raiffeisen, ProCredit, TEB, NLB) and generic banking articles.
negative_findings.result_summary: No evidence found of a non-bank Independent ATM Deployer (IAD) operating a branded ATM estate in Kosovo. ATM deployment appears to sit with banks; processing may be outsourced (e.g. Quipu) but the estate is bank-owned.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell hypothesis that ATM activity is migrating to non-bank independents is not supported for Kosovo on current evidence; the non-bank story here is wallets/EMIs and processing, not ATM estates. Downstream analysis should not assume an IAD segment exists.

negative_findings.description: No licensed Kosovo payment institution or e-money institution was found publishing its own periodic transaction/volume statistics (counts, values, merchant or terminal numbers) on a recurring basis.
negative_findings.result_summary: Actor-level numbers exist only as one-off marketing or partner-press claims (e.g. Quipu's cards/ATM/POS/monthly-transaction figures, Paysera launch claims). Nothing resembling a recurring statistical release from a non-bank licensee was located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's premise that non-bank licensees publish volumes to attract merchants/investors holds only weakly in Kosovo. Non-bank share will have to be inferred from BQK aggregates (digital-wallet series, card/POS series) plus episodic corporate claims, with explicit uncertainty.

negative_findings.description: The canonical BQK list of licensed financial institutions (April 2026 PDF) could not be retrieved: HTTP 403 Forbidden on fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 on https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Lista-e-institucioneve-financiare-22.04.2026-ALB.pdf; the URL is search-indexed and the parent section page is reachable, so this is bot defence rather than a dead link. Recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important actor-map artefact for this cell needs a browser-like fetch path (headers/session) in the collection pipeline; a naive HTTP client will silently produce an empty actor map.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language searching surfaced BQK's own sr publications and terminology but no Kosovo-specific non-bank payment actors, associations or trade press in Serbian.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr queries returned Montenegrin/Bosnian regulators (CBCG, Raiffeisen BiH) and BQK sr documents; no Serbian-language Kosovo fintech/PSP actor sources found. Serbian-language coverage of this cell appears to run through the regulator only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any Serb-majority-municipality payment channels (including parallel/Serbian-dinar cash channels) are invisible to this cell's current source set, which biases cash-usage and non-bank-channel estimates.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo-specific published statistics from the international card schemes (Visa, Mastercard) or from a domestic card switch were located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for a Kosovo domestic card switch/scheme and for scheme-published country volumes returned nothing Kosovo-specific; card acceptance appears to run on Visa/Mastercard via bank and third-party processors with no public country data release.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme-side corroboration of card and POS statistics is unavailable, so BQK remains effectively the sole measurement authority for this market — a single-source dependency worth flagging in any conclusion.

coverage_gaps.description: The definitive per-name list of Kosovo's licensed payment institutions and e-money institutions was not read, because the BQK register PDF returned 403. Named actors in this slice (Paysera Kosova, OneFor, Swinto/Velanis, Numarics) came from press and cluster membership, not from the register itself.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-fetch the dated BQK register PDF with a browser-grade client (or via the ?lang=en section page) and enumerate every non-bank entry; then create one candidate per licensee and cross-verify each against ARBK.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one processor with documented Kosovo operations (Quipu) and one regional vendor (Payten) were identified. The acquiring layer — who actually signs merchants and owns the POS estate in Kosovo — remains largely unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search public procurement (e-prokurimi), bank annual reports and vendor case studies for POS/ATM supply and processing contracts naming Kosovo institutions; also check Compass Plus / TietoEVRY / Asseco SEE customer references.

coverage_gaps.description: No route was established to the audited financial statements of non-bank licensees, which would carry transaction-linked revenue and sometimes volume disclosures.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check whether ARBK or BQK publishes filed annual accounts for IFJB/EMI entities, and whether foreign parents (Paysera LT, OneFor Holding GmbH, Velanis AG, ProCredit Holding for Quipu) disclose Kosovo segment data in home-jurisdiction filings.

coverage_gaps.description: Telecom-led payment channels (Vala/IPKO, Post and Telecom of Kosovo) as non-bank payment or e-money providers were not investigated beyond the postal payment-services page.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run sq/sr searches on mobile-money and telco billing payment services in Kosovo and check whether any telco appears in the BQK non-bank register.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language business media (Telegrafi, Insajderi, Kallxo, Ekonomia Online, albinfo.ch) repeatedly carried the only actor-level numbers found, but no systematic monitoring source was defined for them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a monitored set of Albanian-language business/economy outlets with keyword alerts on 'institucion i parasë elektronike', 'licencë nga BQK', 'pagesa digjitale', 'terminale POS' to catch launch and volume announcements between regulator releases.

brief: Kosovo's non-bank payments landscape is regulator-centric: BQK is simultaneously the licensing authority, the register keeper and effectively the only publisher of quantitative payments data (its 'Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë' report and payment-system time series carry the card, POS, ATM and digital-wallet series). A real non-bank layer exists and is growing under an EU-aligned framework — Paysera Kosova as the first e-money institution, OneFor, Swinto/Velanis and Numarics clustered in the FIKS fintech grouping, with Quipu as the documented card processing and personalisation centre — but, contrary to the cell hypothesis, these actors publish essentially no recurring volume statistics of their own, only episodic launch and partner-press claims. No independent non-bank ATM deployer was found; ATM estates remain bank-owned, so the non-bank story here is wallets, e-money, remittance corridors and outsourced processing rather than terminal ownership. Practical collection should therefore anchor on BQK (register editions, card-usage report, sr-language variants), use ARBK and FIKS to enumerate and disambiguate actors, and treat all actor-level figures as unverified corporate claims.
